reasons.specificity: The inventory precisely captures Elling’s weak-critical thesis, the natural/spiritual-death distinction, and the conceptual-versus-historical modal registers.
reasons.anchoring: Quoted anchors occur in the article and generally support the attributed operators, owners, conditions, warrants, and alternatives.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes necessity of exposure from necessity of unfreedom, conditioned natural death from contingent spiritual death, and conceptual force from historical diagnosis.
reasons.coherence: The prose, modal table, force-change table, and findings ledger consistently preserve the paper’s central scopes and attributions.
reasons.usefulness: The tables provide an inspectable operator inventory with propositions, force, scope, warrant, and alternatives, while the open questions identify genuine limits.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Substantive claims are well supported, but repeated assertions of “complete” coverage are stronger than warranted because several modal claims in the article are omitted or only discussed outside the main inventory.

score.one_line: A highly accurate and useful modal-force inventory, with its main weakness being overclaimed completeness rather than a substantive misreading.
